exercises.translation: Formation task: I am a student. Supply the ordinary polite affirmative nonpast だ/です-series noun ending; no explanatory の/ん ending or honorific alternative.
exercises.evidence: です gives the requested affirmative nonpast noun predicate.
exercises.explanation: The noun itself stays unchanged. です matches the requested polite statement; でした changes the time and ではありません denies the description.

options.label: です
options.rationale: です gives the requested affirmative nonpast noun predicate.

options.label: でした
options.rationale: This is past, not the requested nonpast statement.

options.label: ではありません
options.rationale: This denies the description instead of affirming it.

exercises.translation: Formation task: I was a student then. Supply the ordinary plain affirmative past だ/です-series noun ending, not an explanatory の/ん form.
exercises.evidence: だった supplies the requested past noun predicate.
exercises.explanation: 学生 and 先生 do not acquire case endings. Here the material after the noun marks past time and the requested style. だった is plain; でした would be polite.

options.label: だった
options.rationale: だった supplies the requested past noun predicate.

options.label: だ
options.rationale: This does not mark the requested past time.

options.label: じゃない
options.rationale: This gives a nonpast denial, not a past affirmative.

exercises.translation: Formation task: I am not a student. Supply a polite negative nonpast noun ending. Use the ordinary ありません or ないです endings after では/じゃ, not heightened-polite ございません. The permitted contraction here is では to じゃ; do not add an explanatory の/ん frame.
exercises.evidence: The requested description is negative and nonpast, in polite style.
exercises.explanation: ではありません and じゃありません use the ありません ending; ではないです and じゃないです are also accepted polite negatives, the latter especially conversational. じゃ contracts では. ではございません is a valid more-polite negative, but is outside this explicitly ordinary-ending drill. An affirmative or a past affirmative does not express this denial.

options.label: ではありません
options.rationale: The requested description is negative and nonpast, in polite style.

options.label: です
options.rationale: Affirms the description instead of denying it.

options.label: でした
options.rationale: Says the description was true, not that it is false now.

exercises.translation: Formation task: My older brother is a teacher. Supply the ordinary plain affirmative nonpast だ/です-series noun ending; no explanatory の/ん ending or honorific alternative.
exercises.evidence: だ gives the requested affirmative nonpast noun predicate.
exercises.explanation: The noun itself stays unchanged. だ matches the requested plain statement; だった changes the time and じゃない denies the description.

options.label: だ
options.rationale: だ gives the requested affirmative nonpast noun predicate.

options.label: だった
options.rationale: This is past, not the requested nonpast statement.

options.label: じゃない
options.rationale: This denies the description instead of affirming it.

exercises.translation: Formation task: My older brother was a teacher then. Supply the ordinary polite affirmative past だ/です-series noun ending, not an explanatory の/ん form.
exercises.evidence: でした supplies the requested past noun predicate.
exercises.explanation: 学生 and 先生 do not acquire case endings. Here the material after the noun marks past time and the requested style. でした is polite; だった would be plain.

options.label: でした
options.rationale: でした supplies the requested past noun predicate.

options.label: です
options.rationale: This does not mark the requested past time.

options.label: ではありません
options.rationale: This gives a nonpast denial, not a past affirmative.

exercises.translation: Formation task: My older brother is not a teacher. Supply a plain negative nonpast noun ending. Use the standard ない ending after では/じゃ, not rough contractions of ない such as ねえ. The permitted contraction here is では to じゃ; do not add an explanatory の/ん frame.
exercises.evidence: The requested description is negative and nonpast, in plain style.
exercises.explanation: Both じゃない and the uncontracted ではない give the requested plain negative. The restriction to standard ない excludes rough contractions; plain versus polite is not the same distinction as neutral versus rough. An affirmative or a past affirmative does not express this denial.

options.label: じゃない
options.rationale: The requested description is negative and nonpast, in plain style.

options.label: だ
options.rationale: Affirms the description instead of denying it.

options.label: だった
options.rationale: Says the description was true, not that it is false now.

exercises.translation: Formation task: My older brother will call to my younger sister. Use the basic subject case particle, not topic は or inclusion も.
exercises.evidence: 兄 is the caller in this 呼ぶ pattern.
exercises.explanation: 兄が妹を呼びます makes the older brother the caller and the younger sister the person called. を would mark the brother as an object too; に would not provide the requested subject marking.

options.label: が
options.rationale: 兄 is the caller in this 呼ぶ pattern.

options.label: を
options.rationale: Would mark the brother as an object rather than the caller.

options.label: に
options.rationale: Does not mark the caller as the subject here.

exercises.translation: Formation task: During a room tour you notice: 'The window is large.' Use the basic subject case particle, without topic or inclusion framing.
exercises.evidence: The window is what has the property 大きい.
exercises.explanation: 窓が大きいです describes the window. The subject is not an agent doing something. を does not make the adjective into a transitive verb, and で does not supply this basic subject pattern.

options.label: が
options.rationale: The window is what has the property 大きい.

options.label: を
options.rationale: 大きい does not take the window as a を-marked object.

options.label: で
options.rationale: Does not mark the window as what is large.

exercises.translation: Formation task: My younger sister will read a book. Mark the thing read with the basic object case particle; do not add a topic or 'also' frame.
exercises.evidence: 本 is the thing read, while 妹が is the reader.
exercises.explanation: 本を marks the book as the object of 読む; reading need not physically alter it. 本が would assign subject marking to the book, not mark it as what the sister reads. 本に would not supply this object role.

options.label: を
options.rationale: 本 is the thing read, while 妹が is the reader.

options.label: が
options.rationale: Marks the book as a subject rather than the thing read.

options.label: に
options.rationale: Does not mark the object of 読む in this pattern.

exercises.translation: Formation task: My younger sister will call to my older brother. Mark the person called with the basic object case particle; no topic or inclusion framing.
exercises.evidence: 妹が is the caller; 兄 is the person she calls to.
exercises.explanation: 妹が兄を呼びます makes the sister the caller and the brother the person called. Compare 兄が妹を呼びます, where those roles are reversed. が would mark the brother as another subject, while と would make him a companion in calling, not the person summoned.

options.label: を
options.rationale: 妹が is the caller; 兄 is the person she calls to.

options.label: が
options.rationale: Does not mark the brother as the person called.

options.label: と
options.rationale: Would make the brother a participant in calling together, not the person called.

exercises.translation: Interpretation task: I will read my book. Type the COMPLETE noun phrase marked by を, without を itself; kana is accepted.
exercises.evidence: 私の本 is the complete marked noun phrase.
exercises.explanation: 私の specifies 本; を applies to the whole 私の本, not 私 alone. Kana with わたし or the more formal わたくし is accepted; both represent 私 here. The head alone is shorter than the explicitly requested complete phrase.

options.label: 私の本
options.rationale: 私の本 is the complete marked noun phrase.

options.label: 本
options.rationale: This is only the head, not the complete specified phrase.

options.label: 私
options.rationale: This is the inner modifier, not the complete marked phrase.

exercises.translation: Interpretation task: A teacher at the school will come. Type the COMPLETE noun phrase marked by が, without が itself; kana is accepted.
exercises.evidence: 学校の先生 is the complete marked noun phrase.
exercises.explanation: 学校の specifies 先生; the teacher, not the school building, is coming. The head alone is shorter than the explicitly requested complete phrase.

options.label: 学校の先生
options.rationale: 学校の先生 is the complete marked noun phrase.

options.label: 先生
options.rationale: This is only the head, not the complete specified phrase.

options.label: 学校
options.rationale: This is the inner modifier, not the complete marked phrase.

exercises.translation: Context task: Locate the cat in the garden as something present there, not an event or an activity. Supply one basic case particle, without は/も.
exercises.evidence: This is an ordinary existence-location statement.
exercises.explanation: Use に to locate what is present. が already marks the cat. で would be the activity/event-location pattern, and へ is directional, not the existence-location particle.

options.label: に
options.rationale: This is an ordinary existence-location statement.

options.label: で
options.rationale: This is presence, not an activity/event taking place.

options.label: へ
options.rationale: A direction of movement does not locate what is present.

exercises.translation: Context task: Locate the desk at the library as something present there, not an event or an activity. Supply one basic case particle, without は/も.
exercises.evidence: This is an ordinary existence-location statement.
exercises.explanation: Use に to locate what is present. が already marks the desk. で would be the activity/event-location pattern, and へ is directional, not the existence-location particle.

options.label: に
options.rationale: This is an ordinary existence-location statement.

options.label: で
options.rationale: This is presence, not an activity/event taking place.

options.label: へ
options.rationale: A direction of movement does not locate what is present.

exercises.translation: Context task: I play in the park. Mark the place where this activity happens, not a destination. Use one basic case particle without topic/inclusion.
exercises.evidence: The place is the setting of the stated activity.
exercises.explanation: で locates the playing or reading. に is used for the basic existence-location pattern, but this predicate describes an activity here. へ would indicate a direction, not its setting.

options.label: で
options.rationale: The place is the setting of the stated activity.

options.label: に
options.rationale: Does not supply the activity-location pattern for this verb.

options.label: へ
options.rationale: Does not mark the setting of this playing/reading activity.

exercises.translation: Context task: I read a book at home. Mark the place where this activity happens, not a destination. Use one basic case particle without topic/inclusion.
exercises.evidence: The place is the setting of the stated activity.
exercises.explanation: で locates the playing or reading. に is used for the basic existence-location pattern, but this predicate describes an activity here. へ would indicate a direction, not its setting.

options.label: で
options.rationale: The place is the setting of the stated activity.

options.label: に
options.rationale: Does not supply the activity-location pattern for this verb.

options.label: へ
options.rationale: Does not mark the setting of this playing/reading activity.

exercises.translation: Context task: A class takes place at the school. Locate the event being held, not a physical object. Supply one basic case particle, not a topic/inclusion form.
exercises.evidence: ある means that this class or meeting takes place.
exercises.explanation: で marks the event's location. Compare a desk that exists there: that uses location に. Read the event noun and the sense of ある together, rather than choosing に solely because あります is printed. へ would give a direction, not this event setting.

options.label: で
options.rationale: ある means that this class or meeting takes place.

options.label: に
options.rationale: Uses the physical-presence location pattern rather than the requested event setting.

options.label: へ
options.rationale: Does not locate an event being held.

exercises.prompt: 図書館____会議があります。
exercises.translation: Context task: A meeting takes place at the library. Locate the event being held, not a physical object. Supply one basic case particle, not a topic/inclusion form.
exercises.evidence: ある means that this class or meeting takes place.
exercises.explanation: で marks the event's location. Compare a desk that exists there: that uses location に. Read the event noun and the sense of ある together, rather than choosing に solely because あります is printed. へ would give a direction, not this event setting.

options.label: で
options.rationale: ある means that this class or meeting takes place.

options.label: に
options.rationale: Uses the physical-presence location pattern rather than the requested event setting.

options.label: へ
options.rationale: Does not locate an event being held.

exercises.translation: Context task: I will write a letter with a pen. The named item is the tool, not a companion or recipient. Use one basic particle.
exercises.evidence: The item is the means used to perform the action.
exercises.explanation: で marks the tool. と would not make this tool a participating companion, and に would not express using it as the instrument. English 'with' alone does not choose the particle.

options.label: で
options.rationale: The item is the means used to perform the action.

options.label: と
options.rationale: Does not express the stated tool role.

options.label: に
options.rationale: Does not mark the instrument used for this action.

exercises.translation: Context task: I will cut the paper with scissors. The named item is the tool, not a companion or recipient. Use one basic particle.
exercises.evidence: The item is the means used to perform the action.
exercises.explanation: で marks the tool. と would not make this tool a participating companion, and に would not express using it as the instrument. English 'with' alone does not choose the particle.

options.label: で
options.rationale: The item is the means used to perform the action.

options.label: と
options.rationale: Does not express the stated tool role.

options.label: に
options.rationale: Does not mark the instrument used for this action.

exercises.prompt: 電車____図書館に行きます。
exercises.translation: Context task: I will go to the library by train. Supply the basic particle marking how I travel, with 行く unchanged.
exercises.evidence: The vehicle is the means of travel with 行く.
exercises.explanation: Use 電車で or バスで with 行く. The vehicle takes に in the separate 乗る pattern; it does not follow that every sentence naming a vehicle needs に. と would not describe this means of travel.

options.label: で
options.rationale: The vehicle is the means of travel with 行く.

options.label: に
options.rationale: The vehicle-ni pattern belongs with 乗る, not this means-of-travel use of 行く.

options.label: と
options.rationale: Does not express travelling by the named vehicle.

exercises.translation: Context task: I will go to the school by bus. Supply the basic particle marking how I travel, with 行く unchanged.
exercises.evidence: The vehicle is the means of travel with 行く.
exercises.explanation: Use 電車で or バスで with 行く. The vehicle takes に in the separate 乗る pattern; it does not follow that every sentence naming a vehicle needs に. と would not describe this means of travel.

options.label: で
options.rationale: The vehicle is the means of travel with 行く.

options.label: に
options.rationale: The vehicle-ni pattern belongs with 乗る, not this means-of-travel use of 行く.

options.label: と
options.rationale: Does not express travelling by the named vehicle.

exercises.translation: Context task: I will speak in Japanese. Mark the language used, not a person addressed or words quoted. Use one basic particle. Both language-as-medium and language-as-object framing fit this speaking task.
exercises.evidence: The phrase names the language used for speaking or writing.
exercises.explanation: 日本語で話します presents Japanese as the medium; 日本語を話します makes Japanese the language spoken, the object of 話す. Both fit this task. と and に do not supply the requested language-use pattern in this sentence.

options.label: で
options.rationale: The phrase names the language used for speaking or writing.

options.label: と
options.rationale: Does not mark the language in which the action is performed.

options.label: に
options.rationale: Does not mark the language used here.

additionalCorrectOptions.label: を
additionalCorrectOptions.rationale: 日本語 is the language spoken, the object of 話す; this also fits the visible task.

exercises.translation: Context task: I will write a letter in English. Mark the language used, not a person addressed or words quoted. Use one basic particle.
exercises.evidence: The phrase names the language used for speaking or writing.
exercises.explanation: 英語で specifies the language used to write the letter. 英語を手紙を書きます would give this clause two を phrases instead of preserving 手紙を as the object; the speaking task's を alternative does not transfer here. と and に do not supply the requested language-use pattern in this sentence.

options.label: で
options.rationale: The phrase names the language used for speaking or writing.

options.label: と
options.rationale: Does not mark the language in which the action is performed.

options.label: に
options.rationale: Does not mark the language used here.

exercises.translation: Formation task: I board/ride the train. Supply the basic vehicle case particle selected by 乗る, without topic/inclusion framing.
exercises.evidence: 乗る uses vehicle に in this basic pattern.
exercises.explanation: The vehicle takes に in both 電車に乗ります and the negative バスに乗りません. A factual negative does not change the case pattern or itself imply refusal. Compare 電車で行きます or バスで行きます, which identify the means of going. を is not the basic boarded-vehicle marker with 乗る.

options.label: に
options.rationale: 乗る uses vehicle に in this basic pattern.

options.label: で
options.rationale: This means-of-travel choice does not supply the basic vehicle argument of 乗る.

options.label: を
options.rationale: Does not supply the basic vehicle-ni pattern taught here.

exercises.translation: Formation task: I do not ride the bus. Supply the basic vehicle case particle selected by 乗る, without topic/inclusion framing.
exercises.evidence: 乗る uses vehicle に in this basic pattern.
exercises.explanation: The vehicle takes に in both 電車に乗ります and the negative バスに乗りません. A factual negative does not change the case pattern or itself imply refusal. Compare 電車で行きます or バスで行きます, which identify the means of going. を is not the basic boarded-vehicle marker with 乗る.

options.label: に
options.rationale: 乗る uses vehicle に in this basic pattern.

options.label: で
options.rationale: This means-of-travel choice does not supply the basic vehicle argument of 乗る.

options.label: を
options.rationale: Does not supply the basic vehicle-ni pattern taught here.

spans.gloss: do not board; do not ride

exercises.translation: Context task: I am going to school. Supply a basic destination/route-limit expression with the printed movement verb unchanged. Goal, direction and 'as far as' framing all fit; do not add は/も or mark a starting point.
exercises.evidence: に, へ and まで all fit the destination/route-limit meaning allowed here.
exercises.explanation: に presents the destination as a goal; へ presents movement toward it; まで presents how far the trip extends. All three are accepted for this broad task, not claimed to have identical nuances. 迄 is also accepted as a spelling of まで; kana is the usual beginner model. に/へ alone does not guarantee completed arrival or failure to arrive. から makes the place a starting point; で does not supply this destination role.

options.label: に
options.rationale: に, へ and まで all fit the destination/route-limit meaning allowed here.

options.label: から
options.rationale: Would make this the starting place, not the destination.

options.label: で
options.rationale: Does not mark the requested destination of this movement verb.

additionalCorrectOptions.label: へ
additionalCorrectOptions.rationale: This is the other accepted goal/direction framing with the printed movement verb.

additionalCorrectOptions.label: まで
additionalCorrectOptions.rationale: This marks the trip's extent, which the visible task also permits.

exercises.translation: Context task: I am at the library and ask you, 'Will you come to the library?' Supply a basic destination/route-limit expression with the printed movement verb unchanged. Goal, direction and 'as far as' framing all fit; do not add は/も or mark a starting point.
exercises.evidence: に, へ and まで all fit the destination/route-limit meaning allowed here.
exercises.explanation: に presents the destination as a goal; へ presents movement toward it; まで presents how far the trip extends. All three are accepted for this broad task, not claimed to have identical nuances. 迄 is also accepted as a spelling of まで; kana is the usual beginner model. に/へ alone does not guarantee completed arrival or failure to arrive. から makes the place a starting point; で does not supply this destination role.

options.label: へ
options.rationale: に, へ and まで all fit the destination/route-limit meaning allowed here.

options.label: から
options.rationale: Would make this the starting place, not the destination.

options.label: で
options.rationale: Does not mark the requested destination of this movement verb.

additionalCorrectOptions.label: に
additionalCorrectOptions.rationale: This is the other accepted goal/direction framing with the printed movement verb.

additionalCorrectOptions.label: まで
additionalCorrectOptions.rationale: This marks the trip's extent, which the visible task also permits.

exercises.prompt: 三時____授業が始まります。
exercises.translation: Formation task: Class starts at three. Use the basic time-point case particle, not a range-start, range-end, deadline, topic or inclusion form.
exercises.evidence: The task explicitly requests the clock-time point-marking pattern.
exercises.explanation: に marks the requested time point. A から sentence can also describe when something starts, but it supplies the start-boundary frame excluded by this formation task; it is not universally incorrect. まで would mark an endpoint, and へ is not a time-point marker. This rule does not require に after 今日 or 明日.

options.label: に
options.rationale: The task explicitly requests the clock-time point-marking pattern.

options.label: まで
options.rationale: Marks an endpoint rather than the requested clock-time point.

options.label: へ
options.rationale: Directional へ does not mark a clock time.

exercises.translation: Formation task: I start work at nine. Use the basic time-point case particle, not a range-start, range-end, deadline, topic or inclusion form.
exercises.evidence: The task explicitly requests the clock-time point-marking pattern.
exercises.explanation: に marks the requested time point. A から sentence can also describe when something starts, but it supplies the start-boundary frame excluded by this formation task; it is not universally incorrect. まで would mark an endpoint, and へ is not a time-point marker. This rule does not require に after 今日 or 明日.

options.label: に
options.rationale: The task explicitly requests the clock-time point-marking pattern.

options.label: まで
options.rationale: Marks an endpoint rather than the requested clock-time point.

options.label: へ
options.rationale: Directional へ does not mark a clock time.

exercises.translation: Formation task: I will lend a book to my younger sister. Use the basic borrower case marker in the article's 貸す pattern, not directional, topic or inclusion framing.
exercises.evidence: The named person is the borrower; the thing lent already carries を.
exercises.explanation: The basic pattern is person に + thing を + 貸す. と would make the person a companion in lending, not the borrower; を would make the person another object instead of filling the borrower role. This does not make every に in every predicate a recipient.

options.label: に
options.rationale: The named person is the borrower; the thing lent already carries を.

options.label: と
options.rationale: Would present the person as a companion in lending, not the borrower.

options.label: を
options.rationale: Does not mark the borrower; the lent thing is already marked by を.

exercises.translation: Formation task: I will lend a pen to a friend. Use the basic borrower case marker in the article's 貸す pattern, not directional, topic or inclusion framing.
exercises.evidence: The named person is the borrower; the thing lent already carries を.
exercises.explanation: The basic pattern is person に + thing を + 貸す. と would make the person a companion in lending, not the borrower; を would make the person another object instead of filling the borrower role. This does not make every に in every predicate a recipient.

options.label: に
options.rationale: The named person is the borrower; the thing lent already carries を.

options.label: と
options.rationale: Would present the person as a companion in lending, not the borrower.

options.label: を
options.rationale: Does not mark the borrower; the lent thing is already marked by を.

exercises.translation: Context task: I will write a letter together with a friend. Mark the companion participating with me, not a recipient or a tool. Use one basic particle.
exercises.evidence: The named person takes part with the understood speaker.
exercises.explanation: と marks this companion. 友達に would instead suggest the letter's addressee, not someone writing together with the speaker. で does not mark this one person as the companion in the stated basic pattern.

options.label: と
options.rationale: The named person takes part with the understood speaker.

options.label: に
options.rationale: Does not express the requested companion role.

options.label: で
options.rationale: Does not mark this individual as the companion participating with the speaker.

exercises.evidence: The named person takes part with the understood speaker.
exercises.explanation: と marks this companion. 兄に would not express that the brother travels together with the speaker; 学校に already marks the destination. で does not mark this one person as the companion in the stated basic pattern.

options.label: と
options.rationale: The named person takes part with the understood speaker.

options.label: に

options.label: で
options.rationale: Does not mark this individual as the companion participating with the speaker.

exercises.translation: Formation task: I will buy books and notebooks. Join the two named nouns with the basic noun-list connector, not a representative や/とか list or an additional case marker.
exercises.evidence: と joins these two named nouns before the group's printed case particle.
exercises.explanation: The noun group takes the final を or が as a whole. と names the nouns together; it is not itself an 'only' claim. が and を do not supply the requested link between these nouns. Representative list wording is a different, explicitly excluded task.

options.label: と
options.rationale: と joins these two named nouns before the group's printed case particle.

options.label: が
options.rationale: Would mark a case role, not join these nouns into the requested list.

options.label: を
options.rationale: Would mark an object, not provide the requested noun-list connector.

exercises.explanation: The noun group takes the final を or が as a whole. と names the nouns together; it is not itself an 'only' claim. が and を do not supply the requested link between these nouns. Representative list wording is a different, explicitly excluded task.

exercises.translation: Formation task: My older brother and younger sister will come. Treat 兄と妹 as the named noun list and mark the WHOLE group with the basic subject case particle; no topic/inclusion.
exercises.evidence: Both named people form the subject of 来る.
exercises.explanation: [兄と妹]が来ます gives the full list subject marking. を would not mark the people as the ones coming, and に does not supply that subject role. The inner と and the final が do different jobs.

options.label: が
options.rationale: Both named people form the subject of 来る.

options.label: を
options.rationale: Does not mark the listed people as the subject of 来る.

options.label: に
options.rationale: Does not give the list the requested subject role.

exercises.translation: Formation task: I will buy books and notebooks. Mark the WHOLE named noun group with the basic object case particle; no topic/inclusion.
exercises.evidence: The complete list is what is bought.
exercises.explanation: [本とノート]を買います marks both named items as objects of buying. が would mark the group as a subject, and an extra と would not supply the requested object case. The book and notebook do not become buyers because they stand early in the sentence.

options.label: を
options.rationale: The complete list is what is bought.

options.label: が
options.rationale: Would mark the list as a subject rather than what is bought.

options.label: と
options.rationale: Would not give the complete list the requested object role.

exercises.translation: Formation task: It is a teacher at the school. Supply the single noun-linking particle so that the first noun expression specifies the second; do not form two separate predicates, a relative clause or a noun list.
exercises.evidence: の connects the specifying noun expression to the head noun.
exercises.explanation: The relationship is affiliation, not the school owning a person. N1 の N2 keeps N2 as the main noun. が would make a sentence-level subject relation, not this internal modification. と would name the nouns together, not express the requested relationship.

options.label: の
options.rationale: の connects the specifying noun expression to the head noun.

options.label: が
options.rationale: Does not build the requested noun-modifying phrase.

options.label: と
options.rationale: Would join named nouns rather than express the requested modification.

exercises.explanation: Wood specifies the desk's material, not an owner. N1 の N2 keeps N2 as the main noun. が would make a sentence-level subject relation, not this internal modification. と would name the nouns together, not express the requested relationship.

options.rationale: の connects the specifying noun expression to the head noun.

options.label: が

exercises.translation: Context task: I will walk from home to the station. Mark home as the starting place of this route. Use the basic から/まで range pattern, not a formal source-marker alternative such as より.
exercises.evidence: The blank marks the beginning, not the end, of the stated range.
exercises.explanation: 家から is the start; 駅まで is how far the walk extends. まで would assign an endpoint to the wrong boundary; に would not express the stated from-to range.

options.label: から
options.rationale: The blank marks the beginning, not the end, of the stated range.

options.label: まで
options.rationale: Would mark this boundary as an end rather than the stated start.

options.label: に
options.rationale: Does not supply the from-to starting-boundary relation.

exercises.prompt: 九時____五時まで働きます。
exercises.translation: Context task: I work from nine to five. Mark nine as the starting time of the stated work period. Use the basic から/まで range pattern, not a formal source-marker alternative such as より.
exercises.evidence: The blank marks the beginning, not the end, of the stated range.
exercises.explanation: 九時から supplies the beginning of the period, while 五時まで supplies its endpoint. まで would assign an endpoint to the wrong boundary; に would not express the stated from-to range.

options.label: から
options.rationale: The blank marks the beginning, not the end, of the stated range.

options.label: まで
options.rationale: Would mark this boundary as an end rather than the stated start.

options.label: に
options.rationale: Does not supply the from-to starting-boundary relation.

exercises.translation: Context task: I will walk from home as far as the station. Mark the station as the limit of this route, not a place in which to walk. Supply the basic endpoint expression, without は/も.
exercises.evidence: まで marks the stated range endpoint.
exercises.explanation: 家から駅まで歩きます states a route from home as far as the station. A deadline with までに allows an action to be completed earlier; that is not the requested endpoint relation here. 迄 is an accepted spelling of まで, not a different construction.

options.label: まで
options.rationale: まで marks the stated range endpoint.

options.label: から
options.rationale: Would make the station a starting point instead of the route limit.

options.label: で
options.rationale: Would mark an activity setting, not how far the route extends.

exercises.prompt: 九時から五時____働きます。
exercises.translation: Context task: I work from nine until five. Five ends the stated working period; it is not just a deadline for finishing a separate task. Supply the basic endpoint expression, without は/も.
exercises.evidence: まで marks the stated range endpoint.
exercises.explanation: 九時から五時まで働きます gives the stated work period; it does not specify every break within it. A deadline with までに allows an action to be completed earlier; that is not the requested endpoint relation here. 迄 is an accepted spelling of まで, not a different construction.

options.label: まで
options.rationale: まで marks the stated range endpoint.

options.label: から
options.rationale: Would mark five as another starting boundary.

options.label: までに
options.rationale: Would set a deadline rather than the endpoint of this stated working period.

exercises.prompt: 三時____本を返してください。
exercises.translation: Context task: Please return the book by three. This is a latest-time deadline: earlier completion/arrival is allowed, and the act need not continue until that time. Use the basic まで/までに/に contrast, without topic/inclusion.
exercises.evidence: までに sets the latest permitted time while allowing earlier completion.
exercises.explanation: までに expresses the deadline; 迄に is also accepted, with the same meaning. まで alone gives an until boundary rather than the requested by-deadline pattern. に alone specifies the time, not this explicit latest-time limit allowing an earlier return or arrival.

options.label: までに
options.rationale: までに sets the latest permitted time while allowing earlier completion.

options.label: まで
options.rationale: Does not express the requested by-deadline pattern.

options.label: に
options.rationale: Specifies a time rather than the stated latest-time deadline.

exercises.translation: Interpretation task: I will study at three. Classify the time expression: 時刻 (じこく) = a clock time; 長さ (ながさ) = how long the activity lasts. Type the label or its kana, not a particle.
exercises.evidence: 三時/九時 names a point on the clock.
exercises.explanation: Choose 時刻: this says when, not how many hours. Keep 三時 (three o'clock) distinct from 三時間 (three hours). A duration does not automatically take time-point に.

options.label: 時刻
options.rationale: 三時/九時 names a point on the clock.

options.label: 長さ
options.rationale: That label describes how long, not a clock time.

exercises.translation: Interpretation task: As for this book, I read it. Classify the marked book/fish in this stated reading: 対象 (たいしょう) = what is read/eaten; 主語 (しゅご) = who does the reading/eating; 場所 (ばしょ) = where it happens. Type a label or its kana.
exercises.evidence: The marked noun is what the action applies to, not the person performing it.
exercises.explanation: Choose 対象. は frames the book as a topic/contrast, but the book is still what was read. In these basic object patterns は/も replaces を; it does not turn the object into the subject. The object role is not recoverable from the particle spelling alone.

options.rationale: In the stated reading this noun is not the reader/eater.
